narrative: OMX30 opens with conflicting signals. Global equity weakness (S&P -0.38%, DAX -0.29%) clashes with strong Nikkei (+2.12%) and commodity strength (copper +1.30%, gold +1.06%). The index trades 7.2% above its 200-MA in a bull regime, but MACD has rolled below signal and ADX is critically weak at 9.8—well below the 18 threshold that triggers confidence reduction and 30% magnitude dampening. Yields climbing (+46bp on US 10Y) create a bifurcated setup: banks see wider NIM but tech/real estate face DCF compression. The correlation signal is essentially flat (-0.025%), suggesting no directional tailwind from global macro.
morningBrief: OMX30 enters Monday on thin conviction. ADX at 9.8 forces us to lower confidence and reduce all position magnitudes by 30%—this is a directionless market. Support sits at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance at 3180 (50-MA); yesterday's close 3123 is pivot. USD/SEK +68bp is a genuine positive for Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson on the export side, but NASDAQ weakness (-0.29%) and yield rises create headwinds for tech and real estate. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) should see modest NIM relief; mining (Boliden) rallies on copper strength. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—miss could spike VIX further (already +3.51%). VIX at 15 isn't alarming, but German political headline risk (AfD) may weigh on DAX sentiment and spill into OMX.
